overview: Pertussis, also known as whooping cough, is a highly contagious respiratory tract infection caused by the bacterium Bordetella pertussis. It is characterized by severe coughing fits, often accompanied by a distinctive whooping sound, and can lead to serious complications, especially in infants and young children. The disease can affect people of all ages, but it is most severe in infants under one year of age.
treatment: Antibiotics, such as azithromycin or clarithromycin
Supportive care, such as rest and hydration
transmission: Direct contact with an infected person
prevention: Vaccination with pertussis-containing vaccines, such as DTaP or Tdap
Good hygiene practices, such as washing hands frequently
Avoiding close contact with infected individuals
risk_factors: Infants under one year of age
Young children who are not fully vaccinated
key_facts: Pertussis affects approximately 24.1 million people worldwide each year
The disease is responsible for an estimated 160,700 deaths annually
The majority of pertussis-related deaths occur in infants under one year of age
Vaccination can prevent up to 80% of pertussis cases
The global pertussis vaccination coverage is around 84%
